Sejny Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sejny, Poland

Demolished. Sejny's Jewish population reached its peak in 1885, when Jews accounted for 3,375 of the town's 4,500 residents (75 percent). At the start of WWII, the Germans deported Sejny's Jews to the Lithuanian border; their further fate is unknown. This, the town's first Jewish cemetery, was likely established in the 1880s and used until around 1830 — note the source's own apparent chronological inconsistency between the cemetery's stated founding and closure dates — when a new cemetery was established. It was destroyed during WWII, forgotten afterward, and eventually divided into building plots.
